author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if the opposite of certainty isn’t doubt, but curiosity? Gabrielle Steele reflects on her 21 years inside an apocalyptic cult and how unquestioned beliefs can quietly shape identity, morality, and belonging. Through her personal story and research, she shows how curiosity disrupts inherited certainty and becomes a pathway back to empathy, responsibility, and freedom. 

Gabrielle Steele grew up in a cult — and lived to laugh about it. Now a clinical trials project manager with a master’s in Exercise Physiology, she blends science and satire to explore how we form and fiercely defend our beliefs — in cults, politics, and corporate culture alike. Through humor, resilience, and sharp insight, Gabrielle challenges audiences to question their certainties and trade judgment for curiosity.

When she’s not speaking or writing, she’s mentoring others, riding her bike, and raising two sons — approaching life, like a long ride, with endurance, humility, and a little mischief.

title: How curiosity saved me from a doomsday cult | Gabrielle Steele | TEDxAirlie

description: Who Wrote Your Brain: The Narrative Architecture of Human Belief explores how our thoughts, beliefs, and identity are shaped by family, experiences, education, culture, and the world around us. Swatee Jog explains how the brain turns experiences into stories that influence the way we see ourselves and make decisions. She encourages us to question the beliefs we have carried for years and understand where they came from. The talk shows how changing the stories we tell ourselves can change the way we see possibilities and choices. Ultimately, it invites us to ask: Who wrote the voice inside my head, and which parts of the story will I choose to rewrite? Swatee Jog is the founder of Eeshanya Ventures, a media and branding company. Her journey demonstrates that a smaller city does not have to mean smaller science, lower standards, or lesser opportunities. She also reflects on challenging traditional expectations placed on women and creating an identity through her own work and choices. The talk presents Belagavi as a blueprint for meaningful change—showing that progress begins when we stop asking what we are allowed to do and start asking what needs to be done. Dr. Hitha M. Hebbalkar is a Consulting Dermatologist and founder of Dr. Hebbalkar's Skin & Hair Clinic, Belagavi. Symington drew on an analogy from the Book of Rites: “A parrot may speak, yet it remains a bird.” He argued that generative AI is fundamentally capable of highly efficient imitation, rather than genuine understanding. 
This, he suggested, also offers a reflection on human education: exam-oriented learning can produce students who know how to answer questions without truly understanding them. The ultimate goal of education, he argued, should be to cultivate creative, discerning individuals with a well-rounded character—not efficient algorithms.

Working within the evolving field of cancer research and immunology, she is interested in how the human immune system can be harnessed to develop new approaches to prevention and treatment. Through the buried stories of figures like Enheduanna, history's earliest known named author, and Fu Hao, a warrior-priestess whose tomb lay hidden for over 3,000 years, she makes the case for looking beyond the obvious names we're taught to memorize. My ambition is to become an English teacher and continue my education at a leading university, while exploring opportunities to study and grow internationally.

Alberto Lustosa parte de uma provocação: entre aquilo que uma pessoa fala e aquilo que outra compreende existe uma distância preenchida por experiências, valores, expectativas, medos, crenças e pressuposições. Para demonstrar esse problema, relata um episódio do início de sua carreira como consultor, quando interpretou equivocadamente a solicitação de um cliente e realizou um trabalho adicional que não havia sido contratado. O erro não estava propriamente no que foi dito, mas na certeza de ter compreendido corretamente. Em uma sociedade submetida a informação contínua, telas e estímulos 24 horas por dia, esse problema se intensifica: aprendemos e somos incentivados a falar, argumentar e apresentar nossas posições, mas dedicamos muito menos atenção à capacidade de efetivamente escutar.

title: Você ouviu o que eu falei ou escutou o que eu falei? | Alberto Lustosa | TEDxGoiânia

description:
Gabriel Schimchak parte de sua experiência na organização de dez missões internacionais de inovação, entre 2017 e 2020, para discutir por que empresas e profissionais precisam ultrapassar os limites de seus próprios ambientes para encontrar novas soluções. As missões levaram empresários, executivos, professores e outros participantes a ecossistemas como Israel, China e Vale do Silício, aproximando-os de universidades, startups, incubadoras, centros de pesquisa e grandes empresas de tecnologia. Gabriel observa que muitos gestores permanecem absorvidos pela operação cotidiana, pelas metas, pela burocracia e pelos processos internos de suas organizações, criando uma espécie de bolha que dificulta a inovação. As viagens mostraram que seu principal valor não estava simplesmente em conhecer determinada tecnologia, mas em estabelecer contato direto com pessoas, conhecimentos, culturas e redes capazes de produzir novas possibilidades.

A palestra compara diferentes ecossistemas para mostrar q
title: Buscando a Inovação em Ecossistemas Internacionais | Gabriel Schimchak | TEDxGoiânia

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Celso Camilo inicia sua palestra com uma provocação sobre percepção: diante de um mesmo símbolo sobre uma mesa, uma pessoa pode enxergar o número seis enquanto outra, posicionada no lado oposto, enxerga nove. As duas percepções podem estar corretas dentro de suas perspectivas. A partir desse exemplo, ele questiona a associação automática entre percepção e realidade e recupera Platão e René Descartes para mostrar que a desconfiança em relação aos sentidos não surgiu com a inteligência artificial. Nossos sentidos sempre puderam ser enganados: sabores, aromas, imagens, sons e outras experiências sensoriais podem produzir percepções que não correspondem exatamente àquilo que acreditamos estar diante de nós. A novidade contemporânea, portanto, não é a possibilidade de enganar os sentidos, mas a capacidade tecnológica de fabricar evidências sensorialmente convincentes em escala.

A contribuição central da palestra está na identificação do que efetivamente mudou nessa cadeia perceptiva. Cels
title: 6 e/ou 9 ? | Celso Gonçalves Camilo Junior | TEDxGoiânia

author: TEDx Talks
description:
A palestra de Messias Reis parte de uma mudança fundamental provocada pela inteligência artificial: ver deixou de ser suficiente para crer. Durante séculos, o testemunho ocular, especialmente quando acompanhado por fotografias ou vídeos, funcionou como importante mecanismo de construção de confiança. A IA generativa rompe essa associação ao permitir a criação de evidências convincentes de acontecimentos que nunca existiram. O problema, portanto, não se limita à possibilidade de acreditar em uma falsidade: a disseminação de conteúdos artificiais pode também nos levar a duvidar de evidências verdadeiras. Diante dessa crise de confiança, Messias desloca a questão da capacidade tecnológica de produzir falsificações para um problema essencialmente humano: como preservar autonomia e decidir em que acreditar quando a própria evidência pode ser artificial?

Para responder, Messias recorre à distinção de Daniel Kahneman entre os sistemas 1 e 2 do pensamento. O primeiro opera de maneira rápida,
title: Quando Ver já não Basta | Messias Reis da Silva | TEDxGoiânia

Her books the Ghost from revolutionary past part 1 and part 2 talks about farmers issues, labour rights and queer rights. Her latest book - Mini Dictionary of the LGBTQIA+ community is a dictionary to describe different sexual orientations and genders. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: The Art of Doing Hard Things | Meghna Mehra | TEDxMoulsari Avenue

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Founder & CEO and biotech innovator Dr. Satyabrata Ghosh shares how science can turn perishable harvests into lasting prosperity. In this talk, he unveils how low-cost dehydration and sustainable technologies are reducing food waste, empowering farmers, and building a resilient new rural economy. Dr. Satyabrata Ghosh is a researcher, entrepreneur, and biotechnology professional with over 17 years of experience in scientific research, innovation, and technology development. He holds a Ph.D. in Food Technology and Biochemical Engineering from Jadavpur University and was awarded the prestigious Erasmus Mundus EU Scholarship for advanced research at Universidad Politécnica de Madrid.

He has served as Visiting Faculty at Jadavpur University and as a Research Associate at IIT Kharagpur, with expertise spanning fermentation technology, antioxidants, chemometrics, phage display, and carbohydrate science.

During the COVID-19 pandemic, Dr. Ghosh led the development of a low-cost surgical mask
title: From Dehydration to a New Rural Ecomomy | Dr. Satyabrata Ghosh | TEDxBistupur

author: TEDx Talks
description:
This talk by Space Physics professor Yannis Daglis explores the fascinating, invisible side of our Sun and the 11-year magnetic cycle that shapes life on Earth and beyond.
Beyond the daily light that keeps us alive, the Sun has an invisible magnetic rhythm. Exploring sunspots, solar flares, and powerful solar storms, Daglis explains how these phenomena trigger the northern lights while also putting modern power grids, satellites, and communications at real risk, showing why understanding our star is crucial to protecting life.  Yannis Daglis is a Professor at the University of Athens, a Member of the International Academy of Astronautics, and Greece’s National Representative to international space-related organizations. He served as the first President of the Hellenic Space Center (2020–2025). He has been invited as an expert and evaluator by NASA, the European Commission, and numerous national funding agencies. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but i
title: The cycles of our Sun | Yannis Daglis | TEDxNTUA

author: TEDx Talks
description: "A repetition that hacks the brain", the paradox of music as Dimitris Barmpas states in his talk about the repetitiveness of music. Through this talk Dimitris is describing repeating patterns in the music industry as concentric cycles, starting from single notes and moving all the way up to the big picture of the music history. But why does that happen? Why are those repeating patterns a success recipe and not an "annoying noise"? Can there be something completely new, without repaeating a pattern from the past? Dimitris Barbas (Mr. Music) is a music content creator, vocal coach, and host of the Home Studio Podcast. He creates content centered on music, storytelling, and vocal expression, featuring interviews and in-depth analyses of artists from Greece and abroad, while also approaching music as a powerful tool for inspiration and personal growth. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https:
title: Repetition throughout music history | Dimitris Barmpas | TEDxNTUA

author: TEDx Talks
description:
"Code 0 as the artist’s identity" Through her own journey, Eleni Kavvada reflects on the power of personal signature in a world overwhelmed by information and choices, and the position of the artist within this landscape of data.
Through the story behind her brand 240791, named after her date of birth, Eleni explores how personal codes can emerge unconsciously and become part of a creative identity. In this talk, Cycle 0 becomes a reflection on our own starting point: Do we all need a point zero? Do we build it strategically, or has it always been there, simply waiting for us to give it the attention it deserves? "Eleni Kavvada was born and raised in Athens. She studied fashion design in Milan and Florence. She has completed an internship at the fashion house Salvatore Ferragamo and spent six years working alongside designer Giorgos Eleftheriades.
In 2021, she founded the brand 240791, known for the unconventional silhouettes and volumes of its creations. She has presented her collect
title: Trust your starting point/ 240791 | Eleni Kavvada | TEDxNTUA

author: TEDx Talks
description:
The talk explores architecture as both a process and a narrative. Through the work of Erion Workshop and the format of the series “Architecture for Your Ice Cream”, it presents how architecture is not only the final outcome, but a sequence of decisions, redesigns, and interpretations. At the same time, it highlights the need for architecture to return to the public conversation in a more direct, accessible, and contemporary way. Thanos Ioannidis is an architect and co-founder of the design-build practice Erion Workshop. Through his studio, he creates architectural narratives that he follows from the first sketches to their construction. At the same time, together with Chara Kontochristou, he created the series “Architecture for Your Ice Cream”, with the aim of bringing architecture back into public discussion and closer to social media platforms.

Chara Kontochristou is a content creator who first became known through her POV vlogs and is now involved in a range of different content p
title: Crafting Architecture Stories | Thanos Ioannidis & Chara Kontochristou | TEDxNTUA

author: TEDx Talks
description:
"In healthcare, we don’t judge technology only as users—we judge it as children, parents, and caregivers," Nassos Katsamanis shares as he investigates what happens when AI answers the phone at overcrowded medical clinics.
While many feared that older people would struggle with the automated system, patient data revealed an unexpected truth: elderly callers felt heard and unhurried for the first time in years. In this talk, Katsamanis unpacks how empathy in healthcare technology isn't about warm words, but patient pacing, active listening, and designing systems that support the entire caregiving ecosystem. Nassos Katsamanis is a researcher and entrepreneur in the field of artificial intelligence, with a focus on voice technologies and human-machine interaction. He is the co-founder of Auxilis AI, where he develops voice-based digital assistants aimed at improving access to healthcare. He also holds a PhD in Electrical Engineering from the National Technical University of Athens (NTUA)
title: When AI Answers the Doctor’s Phone | Nassos Katsamanis | TEDxNTUA

author: TEDx Talks
description:
"Greek islands are not our problem, they are our laboratories," Stergios Vakalis shares as he explores the balance between resource limits, seasonal pressure, and innovation.
In this talk, standard top-down solutions are challenged by the reality of isolated systems. Composting in Tinos, energy storage in Ikaria, and vehicle-to-grid tech in Astypalaia, Stergios introduces "Cycle 0", the crucial initial stage of testing, learning, and iterating to build truly resilient, circular, and community-driven futures. Stergios Vakalis is an Assistant Professor of Energy Processes at the School of Chemical Engineering of the National Technical University of Athens. His work focuses on energy analysis, thermochemical biofuel production, and energy systems modeling. His research also emphasizes the energy transition of island regions and the development of sustainable, “green” island systems. He is a member of the Editorial Board of the scientific journal Nature Scientific Reports (Springer). This
title: Cycle 0: Restarting islands, restarting systems | Stergios Vakalis | TEDxNTUA

author: TEDx Talks
description: "Every story completes a cycle" Journalist Elena Papadimitriou explores how news is created, verified, and received, revealing that journalism does not end with publication but continues through the questions, choices, and feedback of its audience. In this talk, "Cycle 0" is reflected in the continuous relationship between information and those who produce and consume it. Alongside the story of news, Elena shares her own journey in journalism, reflecting on the moments that have renewed her passion for the profession, time and again. Elena is a journalist. She studied Journalism at the Aristotle University of Thessaloniki and holds a Master’s degree in Political Science and Sociology from the National and Kapodistrian University of Athens. She has been working for 25 years, mainly in television and radio, focusing on news and current affairs programmes. She has covered elections, referendums and humanitarian crises through journalistic assignments outside Greece. In 2025, she received
title: Collect, Report, Repeat: Every story completes its own cycle | Elena Papadimitriou | TEDxNTUA

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Sometimes you need a setback in order to move forward stronger. Four-time Olympian swimmer Nora Drakou shares her story about athleticism and the importance of the power of the mind. In her talk she uncovers all of the feelings going through the mind of a young athlete ready to conquer the pool when suddenly injuries knock on the door. But that's how life goes sometimes. "These injuries weren't a setback, they were the only way to discover my own strength"; because the strong one is the one "who learned to swim along with its imperfections". "Nora Drakou is a swimmer who has competed in four Olympic Games. She is a two-time European medalist and a finalist at the World Championships in 2013 and 2024. In addition, she has won nine Mediterranean medals and holds forty Greek national records.
She has recorded the most victories in Greek National Championships in the history of Greek swimming. She has been a member of the Greek National Team since 2008, and in 2027 she will celebrate twen
title: The power of coming back | Nora Drakou | TEDxNTUA

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Dimitris Samolis shares his perspective about the similarities of concepts that may look distant but they are oddly similar - as if they were the first and the last spots of an imaginary circle. Comic and tragic, trauma and miracle, bully and bullied, success and failure, insecurity and confidence. Through his personal experiences he analyses the aspects of each of these circles focusing on ways in which we can break free of those cycles and heal our souls; or even try to cover our wounds with beautiful sequenced fabrics. "Dimitris Samolis is an actor, singer and songwriter. A graduate of the National Theatre of Greece Drama School as well as the Athens Law School, he has participated in numerous productions, including performances at the Epidaurus Festival and the National Theatre, as well as television series such as ""Agries Melisses"" and ""Floga kai Anemos"".
He has released four personal music albums: one in English: ""Popetry"" (2015), and three in Greek: ""Ena Siban Sta Metra
title: The revolution of glitter | Dimitris Samolis | TEDxNTUA

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if the fear, anxiety, or hesitation you experience today isn't really about today at all? 

In this powerful TEDxSFIT Talk, author and emotional intelligence expert Parinita Kothari shares her deeply personal journey of grief, resilience, and emotional healing. After losing her mother in a sudden car accident, she spent 17 years convincing herself to "stay strong" only to discover that unprocessed emotions had quietly shaped every major decision she made. 

Through the unforgettable Dung Beetle analogy, Parinita reveals why we carry emotional burdens for years, how unresolved experiences influence our choices, and why learning to process our emotions is the first step toward living with greater freedom, clarity, and courage. 
 Parinita Kothari is a best-selling author, Growth Coach, and the Founder of Petricore Mindworks. With over 20 years of leadership experience, she empowers professionals to become emotionally intelligent, purpose-driven leaders by blending neuroscience, psyc
title: The Dung Beetle Effect: How Unprocessed Grief Holds You Back | Parinita Kothari | TEDxSFIT

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Lorenzo D'Agostino invita a guardare oltre i luoghi comuni che circondano il tema delle migrazioni.
Attraverso dati, inchieste e testimonianze mostra come molte narrazioni sull'immigrazione siano lontane dalla realtà e analizza il funzionamento delle politiche di frontiera, evidenziandone limiti e contraddizioni.
Il suo intervento propone una riflessione radicale sul significato stesso dei confini, interrogandosi su come possano diventare strumenti di tutela invece che di esclusione. Giornalista investigativo freelance specializzato in migrazioni e politiche di frontiera nel Mediterraneo. Le sue inchieste sono state pubblicate da numerose testate internazionali, tra cui The Intercept, Libération, El País, Internazionale, CNN e Der Spiegel.
Negli ultimi anni si è concentrato sulle questioni giudiziarie legate all’immigrazione, in particolare sull’abuso della legislazione antimafia in Italia per la criminalizzazione di migranti e operatori umanitari. A settembre 2025 ha partecipato alla
title: Tutto quello che credi di sapere sull'immigrazione è falso | Lorenzo D’Agostino | TEDxMessina

author: TEDx Talks
description:
You can see a scar. You can't always see what it took to get there.

Through her experience with chronic illness, recovery, and the pressure to keep showing up, Kashisha explores the grief we leave unspoken, and why our circumstances may shape how we move, but never how big we are allowed to dream. Kashisha Goel is a Grade 12 IB Diploma student at Chatrabhuj Narsee School, a dancer, a writer, and someone who geeks out over marketing. Fascinated by why people believe what they believe and buy what they buy, she co-founded Project Synapse, making neuroscience, psychology, and neuromarketing accessible through research and workshops, and founded FinePrint, a social enterprise transforming children's artwork into products with NGO partners while ensuring artists receive credit and profit shares. She researches consumer psychology, serves as Managing Editor of her school newsletter, has written for Teenager Today, Elite Gazette, and Centsible Education, interned at Eggfirst Advertising, an
title: The Grief Nobody Names | Kashisha Goel | TEDxCNS Mumbai Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
The Functioning Excuse, the quiet rule that says our struggles don't count as long as we're still delivering, still performing, still saying yes.
Argument: Not "students are stressed and hide it," everyone knows that. The sharper point: competence itself becomes the disguise. When you fall apart quietly while still performing, people don't see someone in trouble, they see someone to admire. And the deepest cost isn't hiding the pain from others; it's that after years of telling yourself nothing counts, you lose the ability to feel it yourself.
 Shambhavi Pendke is a Mumbai-based student, writer, and founder drawn to the intersection of finance, entrepreneurship, and social impact. She has won international awards, earned academic scholarships, founded her own venture, and led as a captain and national-level speaker, building a track record that, from the outside, looks like someone who has it all together. But those same experiences are exactly what taught her the pressure of always s
title: The Functioning Excuse | Shambhavi Pendke | TEDxCNS Mumbai Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if the chapter you are struggling through is not the end of your story, but the beginning of a new version of you?

Through a deeply personal journey of setbacks, self-doubt, resilience, and reinvention, this talk explores the silent struggles we often carry while growing up, and the courage it takes to move forward when life does not go as planned.

One difficult chapter does not define the whole story, and every time we choose to begin again, we discover new versions of ourselves.

Because your current chapter is not your final story.

The Unsaid Richa Pendake is a corporate leader turned entrepreneur, the Founder and CEO of Nutrizoe, and a proud mother of two daughters. Today, Nutrizoe has impacted over 300,000 mothers and has been a part of Shark Tank India Season 4, recognised by the Times of India's Most Valued Mother & Child Brand award, Amazon Launchpad, the Nestlé Accelerator Program, and YourStory's Top 100 D2C Challenger Brands. She holds patents and proprietary blends
title: The Unsaid: Beginning Again | Richa Pendake | TEDxCNS Mumbai Youth
